item.title: B.C. expands firefighters’ compensation coverage by adding eight cancers to list
item.description: VICTORIA — British Columbia has expanded its compensation coverage for firefighters in the province by adding eight cancers to the list of eligible illnesses. The province says the additions to the list of diseases “presumed to be linked to the work done by firefighters” make B.C. the most comprehensively covered Canadian province. The newly added […]

item.title: Peace pickleball players enjoy success at Grande Prairie tournament
item.description: Pickleball players from B.C. and Alberta descended on the new Paddle Club in Grande Prairie for an opening tournament on February 27th and 28th.

item.title: Fort St. John council pens open letter requesting return of seniors housing funding
item.description: Fort St. John council has voted to pen a letter demanding the return of funding for a senior housing project in the city.

item.title: Blueberry River First Nations members’ pipeline protest shunned by chief and council
item.description: Protesters and contractors from Blueberry River First Nations (BRFN) set up a road blockade north of Fort St. John on Monday, March 2nd to protest the NEBC Connector project, but BRFN chief and council do not condone the action.

item.title: B.C.’s move to end clock changes won’t be without complications
item.description: British Columbia Premier David Eby announced on Monday, March 2nd that the province will be moving to permanent daylight time.

item.title: Fort St. John craft brewery up for sale
item.description: Beard's Brewing Company, which started out life as a craft brewery in downtown Fort St. John in 2017, is up for sale.

item.title: MLAs continue calls for full public inquiry into Tumbler Ridge tragedy
item.description: Two MLAs, including Peace River South MLA Larry Neufeld, continue to call for a full public inquiry into the February 10th mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge, after a coroner's inquest was announced on March 3rd.

item.title: City seeks proposals for sponsor naming rights for recreation locations
item.description: The City of Fort St. John is asking businesses to come forward with proposals for the renaming of several recreation assets, including the Pomeroy Sport Centre, by April 2nd.

item.title: Fort St. John family fears autism support funding cut under eligibility changes
item.description: A parent in Fort St. John is concerned for her daughter's future after the province made changes to autism funding.

item.title: Mideast war driving up Europe natural gas prices, highlighting Canada’s potential
item.description: The widening war in the Middle East is driving up spot natural gas prices in Europe and Asia, highlighting the potential for Canada to play a greater role as a stable global supplier.
